title: The DISRPT 2019 Shared Task on Elementary Discourse Unit Segmentation and Connective Detection
research_question: How accurately can shared-task systems identify elementary discourse-unit boundaries and exact explicit-connective spans across multilingual discourse corpora under treebanked and plain-tokenized input conditions?
methodology: A shared-task overview compares representative submissions on multilingual RST/SDRT EDU boundary segmentation and PDTB explicit-connective detection. Each task has treebanked and plain-tokenized input settings. The authors report positive-class precision, recall, and F1, micro-averaged within corpora and macro-averaged across corpora. Four teams address EDU segmentation; three address connective detection in at least one setting. For teams with multiple systems, the best macro-F1 system is selected. ToNy and IXA use RNNs with embeddings, DFKI RF uses tree ensembles with linguistic features, and GumDrop combines approaches. This overview does not independently isolate the causal effects of architecture, syntax, sentence boundaries, or data size.

key_findings.finding: The paper defines EDUs as nonoverlapping discourse-tree building blocks, mostly sentences or clauses, with exceptions for complement and restrictive clauses; this is its annotation-unit definition, not a comparison of units for work matters.
key_findings.quote: EDUs or Elementary Discourse units are non- overlapping “minimal building blocks of a discourse tree” (Carlson et al., 2003).
key_findings.evidence_basis: Documented definition, corroborated by the single-boundary encoding in section 2; no empirical claim that this is the optimal semantic unit.

key_findings.finding: The shared task uses 15 corpora in 10 languages: 12 EDU-segmentation corpora under RST/SDRT and 3 explicit-connective corpora under PDTB; corpus inventory counts are not test-set denominators.
key_findings.quote: 15 datasets in 10 languages, 12 of which tar- get elementary discourse unit segmentation, and 3 dedicated to explicit connective annotation.

key_findings.finding: Treebanked input includes linguistic annotations with corpus-dependent gold quality; plain input retains tokenization and document boundaries but omits sentence splits, POS, and supplied parses.
key_findings.quote: data (*.conll), which included an (ideally gold) dependency parse, including gold sentence splits and POS tags, and unannotated, plain tokens (*.tok).
key_findings.evidence_basis: Input specification and explicit corpus qualifications.

key_findings.finding: EDU precision, recall, and F1 score positive boundary locations only; scores pool decisions within each corpus and then macro-average across corpora separately for each system and input scenario.
key_findings.quote: scores reward only the positive classes, i.e. precision and recall of segmentation is judged purely based on identification of segmenta- tion points, with no reward for recognizing nega- tive cases.
key_findings.evidence_basis: Stated scorer protocol; this is boundary F1, not EDU exact-span F1, token accuracy, or Topic quality.

key_findings.finding: Connective detection evaluates exact spans and gives no partial credit; the example with an extra predicted token incurs one false-positive span and one false-negative span.
key_findings.quote: it misses the gold span and invents one not present in gold data.
key_findings.evidence_basis: Explicit scoring example, not an observed error-rate estimate.
key_findings.qualification: The prose describes both precision and recall as calculated out of gold spans. Preserve this imprecision; standard precision uses predicted spans and recall uses gold spans. The scorer code was not inspected.

key_findings.finding: On the 12 EDU test corpora with treebanked input, Table 2 reports macro F1 of 90.11 for ToNy, 88.11 for GumDrop, 87.41 for IXA, and 84.58 for DFKI RF. ToNy leads on 8 corpora, GumDrop on 3, and DFKI RF on 1.
key_findings.evidence_basis: Table 2 and section 3.1; all scores are on the paper’s 0–100 scale.
key_findings.qualification: ToNy’s reported average is over five nondeterministic runs; uncertainty intervals are absent. Prose conflicts for IXA and DFKI RF are retained as U01-I01.

key_findings.finding: On the 12 EDU test corpora with plain-tokenized input, Table 3 reports macro F1 of 86.38 for ToNy, 83.89 for GumDrop, and 68.5 for DFKI RF. ToNy leads on 11 corpora; on zho.rst.sctb GumDrop reaches 73.13 versus ToNy 65.26.
key_findings.evidence_basis: Table 3; no IXA result is reported for this setting.

key_findings.finding: For exact connective detection on tur.pdtb.tdb in the shared-task evaluation, treebanked F1 is 69.85 for ToNy and 79.19 for GumDrop; plain-input F1 is 85.37 and 79.17, respectively. Thus the input-setting comparison is system- and corpus-dependent.
key_findings.evidence_basis: Table 4, with the Turkish reversal explicitly discussed in section 3.2.
key_findings.qualification: Section 3.2 reports robustness across five ToNy runs and deterministic seeding for GumDrop; no per-run values or significance test are supplied. Table 4 split is inferred to be the shared-task test evaluation from the results context, rather than separately restated in its caption.

key_findings.finding: Section 3.1 asserts that the treebanked EDU macro F1 is 87.18 for IXA and 84.56 for DFKI RF.
key_findings.quote: IXA (Iruskieta et al. 2019, 87.18 F1) and DFKI RF (Bourgonje and Schäfer 2019, 84.56 F1).
key_findings.evidence_basis: These asserted means conflict with Table 2’s 87.41 and 84.58; the PDF visibly contains both sets of values.
key_findings.qualification: Arithmetic means of the 12 displayed per-corpus F1 values reproduce the table means. The paper supplies no alternate mean definition or explanation; ordinary two-decimal rounding is insufficient. See U01-I01.

key_findings.finding: The authors infer that syntax is not central to connective detection and that more data improve inventory coverage; these explanations are not established by a controlled syntax or data-size ablation in this overview.
key_findings.quote: syntax is not central to the task (tree- banked and plain results are close)
key_findings.evidence_basis: Author interpretation of cross-corpus and cross-scenario scores; language, guidelines, system, and input quality vary together.
key_findings.qualification: The scores support the specific measured comparisons in U01-F08, not a general causal or business-email conclusion.

limitations: U01 evaluates discourse units and connective spans. It supplies no direct business-email Topic-assignment, overlap, discontinuity, action/reply scope, or decision-bearing preservation result (U01-F01–F05; topic02.not_evaluated_for_msgloom).

The corpora differ in language, framework, guideline, size, and linguistic-input quality. Cross-corpus score differences are not controlled transfer or annotation-unit comparisons (U01-F02–F03; section 2, raw lines 199–236; section 4, lines 419–433).

This overview does not report IAA statistics, annotator counts, adjudication details, split unit/counts, or duplicate/near-duplicate and leakage controls. Their absence is missing documentation, not evidence that the datasets lack such controls (topic02.inter_annotator_agreement and split_and_leakage).
The numerical and protocol ambiguities U01-I01–I05 remain explicit. The PDF resolves extraction questions but does not explain the conflicting means.

No variance estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests accompany the score tables. Five ToNy runs and deterministic GumDrop seeding are mentioned, without per-run results (raw lines 295–303 and 385–397).

Architecture explanations are observational in this paper. The attributed effects of embeddings, whole-document context, tree-ensemble robustness, or syntax are hypotheses rather than controlled ablation findings (U01-F10; raw lines 434–466).

Historical comparisons cite prior studies, sometimes on explicitly different corpora. Those studies and their scoring/split comparability were not independently examined (raw lines 328–338 and 368–376).

reproducibility.availability_scope: Frozen paper-reported availability in 2019, not a current availability check. code_available refers to the shared-task evaluation and text-reconstruction scripts; it does not assert that all submitted model source code was released.
reproducibility.data_access: The paper reports a uniform-format dataset release. Four corpora have only annotations with underscore tokens in the public repository. Reconstruction requires access to the original LDC releases; the overview does not enumerate all four affected corpora.
reproducibility.model_code_and_execution: The paper refers to the system papers, but this analysis did not inspect or execute model code. Hyperparameters, dependency versions, hardware cost, latency, and exact runtime reproduction commands are not supplied here.
reproducibility.randomness: The treebanked ToNy mean is explicitly described as averaged over five runs due to nondeterministic GPU training; section 3.2 reports the Turkish connective reversal persisting over five ToNy runs and deterministic GumDrop seeding. No run dispersion is reported.

confidence_score_semantics: Confidence in the finding as a supported substantive claim, not a significance probability. F09 has high transcription certainty but low confidence as the asserted numerical result because Table 2 contradicts it. F10 has limited causal support.

evaluated_tasks.exact_target: Locate the beginning token of each EDU; evaluate boundary points, not topic boundaries or exact EDU spans.
Retrieve exact spans of explicit connectives under a single BI/outside token-label sequence; this is not exact Topic-span assignment.

annotation_unit.EDU: A nonoverlapping discourse terminal, mostly a sentence or clause, except complement and restrictive clauses; corpus-specific guidelines remain different.
annotation_unit.connective: An explicit connective expressed as a token span, with Begin/Inside labels; no Topic identifier or discourse-relation argument target is defined for this shared task.
annotation_unit.encoding: CoNLL-U MISC uses BeginSeg=Yes for EDU starts, Seg=B-Conn and Seg=I-Conn for connectives, and _ for outside/unannotated tokens. SpaceAfter supports whitespace information in the treebanked representation.
annotation_unit.section: PDF pages 1 and 3, section 1 footnote 1 and section 2; Figure 1 visually inspected
source_sections: section 2 and Figure 1, selected visual transcription

prediction_unit.EDU: One boundary/no-boundary decision at each token position, inducing an ordered partition of the document token stream.
prediction_unit.connective: One B-Conn/I-Conn/outside state at each token, decoded into exact connective spans.
prediction_unit.context_is_separate: ToNy can use a whole document or large chunk as context; this does not change the output into document Topics or non-sequential Topic clusters.
prediction_unit.status: The partition/cardinality implications are analyst interpretations of the documented encoding and task; the paper does not enumerate every model decoder constraint.

contiguity.gold: The shared-task EDU boundary representation yields consecutive nonoverlapping units. BI connective labels describe contiguous spans in the evaluated representation.
contiguity.prediction: The reported tasks recover that linear representation. They do not identify recurring Topics or link non-sequential clusters.
contiguity.scope_limit: This concerns the exported shared-task targets; it is not a claim that every underlying RST/SDRT/PDTB annotation layer or linguistic connective has the same capability.

gold.EDU: Binary start/no-start labels; each token lies in one induced EDU, not in several Topic memberships.
gold.connective: One B/I/outside target per token; a document may contain multiple connective spans, with no multi-Topic label set.

prediction.EDU: One boundary decision per token in the evaluated representation.
prediction.connective: Single BIO-style sequence; multiple memberships for the same token are not represented or scored.

label_cardinality.topic_cardinality: Neither gold nor predicted Topic memberships exist in this evaluation. Multiple EDUs in a document do not show that one message is assigned to several Topics.
label_cardinality.status: Encoding-derived interpretation, not a separate multi-label experiment.

within_one_message.gold: No one-Topic identifier linking separated spans within a message is described or evaluated. EDU starts and BI tags provide no such link.
within_one_message.prediction: No prediction or scoring of separated pieces as one Topic is reported.

thread_level.gold: No email thread-level Topic chains, cross-message semantic identities, or interleaved-Topic cluster gold is evaluated.
thread_level.prediction: No corresponding thread-level or cross-Source linkage task is reported.

discontinuity.connective_qualification: The overview supplies no discontinuous-connective object encoding or separate discontinuous-span evaluation; do not infer a capability from the underlying PDTB formalism.

gold.connective: Single BI/outside encoding; overlapping connective membership is not described as a gold target.
gold.Topic: Unsupported as a task capability; no Topic gold is evaluated.

prediction.EDU: A boundary-induced partition cannot assign one token to overlapping EDUs.
prediction.connective: The documented output sequence does not express multiple overlapping memberships.

overlap.scope: No conclusion about overlapping labels in other annotation layers or other papers.

material_inconsistencies.resolution: Both values were verified in the original PDF. Recalculation reproduces Table 2 at two decimals. The prose values cannot follow from ordinary rounding of those cells; no alternate mean definition is given. Retain both, and use explicitly table-labeled values only.

material_inconsistencies.setting: Exact connective spans, Table 4 shared-task evaluation; macro over eng.pdtb.pdtb, tur.pdtb.tdb, zho.pdtb.cdtb, 0–100 scale
material_inconsistencies.resolution: PDF verified. Deviations exceed ordinary two-decimal rounding. The paper provides no explanation; do not silently replace the printed means. Rankings of the reported best systems are unchanged by this arithmetic check.

material_inconsistencies.setting: Rightmost Mean columns of EDU Tables 2 and 3, across displayed systems within each corpus
material_inconsistencies.details: These columns are not defined in the prose. They do not consistently equal either the arithmetic mean of displayed F1 values or the harmonic mean of displayed mean precision and recall. They are distinct from the explicitly defined per-system macro-over-corpora score.
material_inconsistencies.resolution: Preserve these values as printed with an unspecified definition. Do not use them as comparative performance evidence.

material_inconsistencies.setting: Exact connective-span precision and recall, section 2
material_inconsistencies.paper_wording: The prose assigns both precision and recall to total gold connective spans; Example (1) separately describes a precision error for an invented span and a recall error for a missed gold span.
material_inconsistencies.resolution: Record the paper wording and the example. Standard PRF interpretation uses predicted spans for precision and gold spans for recall; this interpretation is not a verified scorer implementation. No claim that both denominators were actually gold.

material_inconsistencies.details: Section 2 uses ideally gold syntax and describes gold sentence splits, whereas section 4 names automatic parses and automatic sentence segmentation in some treebanked corpora. Plain input is also called automatically parsed data in section 3.1, although section 2 supplies only tokenized text and document boundaries.
material_inconsistencies.resolution: Use treebanked as the setting name, with corpus-specific annotation quality. Use plain tokenized for the supplied input; do not imply a common supplied automatic parser or universal gold syntax.

RQ1.support: Annotation-unit transfer only: EDU definition and boundary recovery are useful candidates, without evidence that EDUs preserve a Topic’s full scope.

RQ2.support: No direct email/asynchronous Topic-cluster or interleaving evaluation.

RQ3.support: No Topic membership gold or predictions; only limits of the EDU/BI representation can be inferred.

RQ4.support: No direct or evaluated transfer result for overlapping/discontinuous Topic assignment.

RQ5.support: No measured work-scope preservation; boundary and connective errors motivate an untested preservation audit.

RQ6.support: Strong task-specific scoring documentation, with retained aggregation and denominator ambiguities. No metric equivalence to Topic segmentation.

RQ7.support: Corpus inventory, input-quality differences, access restrictions and missing split/IAA controls constrain unit transfer.

RQ8.support: Motivates a unit comparison and boundary-source ablation on reviewed work text; no architecture approval.

interpretation.text: Treat EDU segmentation as a candidate preprocessing unit with recoverable source offsets. The reported scores do not show that one EDU equals one Topic or that discourse relations preserve work scope.
Separate sentence-split quality, parse provenance, language, and corpus guideline when assessing transfer. A treebanked-versus-plain difference does not isolate syntax alone.

Retain uncertainty about causes. Whole-document context, contextual embeddings, and tree ensembles are plausible factors discussed by the authors, without controlled ablation evidence in U01. The zho.rst.sctb treebanked DFKI advantage called substantial in section 4 is only 0.40 F1 points in Table 2 (81.67 versus 81.27); no significance test is supplied.

proposed_experiments.status: untested msgloom research proposal, not approved architecture
proposed_experiments.question: Which candidate unit preserves reviewed work-matter evidence and scope?
proposed_experiments.design: On the same user-reviewed or synthetic work-message sample, compare sentence, clause, EDU, and arbitrary-span/hybrid candidates. Preserve original text offsets. Annotate Topic identities separately, allowing multiple memberships and separated pieces; never force one Topic per EDU.
proposed_experiments.evaluation: Report unit-boundary scores separately from Topic span assignment. Measure omitted or broadened conditions, evidence, exceptions, approval scope, action scope, and reply scope against reviewed evidence bundles. Record disagreements and uncertain assignments.

proposed_experiments.status: untested msgloom research proposal, not approved architecture
proposed_experiments.question: How much error comes from sentence boundaries and syntax before semantic assignment?
proposed_experiments.design: Use matched messages and the same downstream task with gold versus predicted sentence boundaries and separately controlled parse inputs. Compare EDU recovery and work-scope preservation; keep message/thread groups and near duplicates separated between development and evaluation.
proposed_experiments.evaluation: Report within-sentence and sentence-initial boundary errors separately, then independent preservation and Topic-assignment metrics. Do not interpret a single boundary F1 as end-to-end success.

proposed_experiments.status: untested msgloom research proposal, not approved architecture
proposed_experiments.question: Can grouping candidate EDUs recover non-contiguous or overlapping evidence without broadening scope?
proposed_experiments.design: Construct reviewed cases with one work matter interrupted by another, a span supporting multiple matters, and a reply that answers only one condition. Evaluate an additional evidence-linking layer while retaining all original content and explicit uncertainty.
proposed_experiments.evaluation: Separate gold representation capacity from predicted assignment quality; report within-message discontinuity and thread-level recurrence as different strata. This is a new task beyond U01, not a claimed capability of DISRPT models.
